evidence_frontier: The latest completed evidence confirms that a local width of 8 (w8) meets the preregistered gate against the w16 control after 100 epochs on ECG200 (aggregate correct 444 vs 448). Earlier 100‑epoch runs with w12 showed aggregate correct 884 versus 897 for w16 but were not confirmed because the gate was not preregistered for that comparison. No experiment has yet tested w12 against the w16 control on a fresh seed set, leaving the robustness of the intermediate width unknown.
analysis: Observations: (1) w8 passes the accuracy gate versus w16 after 100 epochs on ECG200. (2) w12 previously achieved slightly lower aggregate correct (884) than w16 (897) on the same dataset but with the same seed set used for discovery, not a fresh confirmation. (3) The gate for confirmation must compare candidate to concurrent control on the same fresh seeds. Hypothesis: If the local width is set to 12, the model will retain performance within 10 correct predictions of the w16 control on a new seed set, indicating that intermediate compression does not materially degrade Q.ANT accuracy or numerical agreement.
hypothesis: A local width of 12 will achieve aggregate Q.ANT correct predictions within ten of the w16 control (i.e., >= w16_correct‑10) on a fresh five‑seed set after 100 epochs, demonstrating that intermediate compression is robust.

proposal.title: 100‑epoch w12 Confirmation on ECG200
proposal.research_question: Does a local width of 12 maintain comparable Q.ANT accuracy and numerical agreement to the 16‑width control under a fresh seed set, indicating robustness of intermediate compression?
proposal.rationale: w8 has been validated as the minimal viable width, but the behavior of intermediate widths remains untested. Confirming w12 on an independent seed set will map the width‑performance curve, informing future model size trade‑offs without claiming w12 as the new minimum. This experiment is novel because it uses a seed set not previously employed and directly compares w12 to the w16 control under the same conditions.

procedure: Train each candidate on the ECG200 training set for 100 epochs
Evaluate Q.ANT predictions on the ECG200 test set
Record aggregate correct predictions and mean absolute logit error for each candidate
Apply the preregistered gate: w12.aggregate_qant_correct >= w16.aggregate_qant_correct - 10

proposal.success_criteria: The experiment passes if the w12 candidate achieves aggregate Q.ANT correct >= (w16 aggregate correct - 10) on the five‑seed set. Additionally, the mean absolute logit error for w12 must not exceed that of w16 by more than 0.005, ensuring comparable numerical agreement.
proposal.risks: Potential risks include stochastic variance causing the gate to fail despite true equivalence, limited seed count reducing statistical power, and the possibility that w12 performance degrades beyond the gate threshold, which would require revisiting compression strategies. All measurements remain in Q.ANT CPU/software simulation, avoiding hardware‑level claims.
